A qualifying child under age 13 whom you can claim as a dependent ... 3. Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent"; p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). The line reads dependent.dc_qp, inside the invalid closure. By reading the box test is the project's for a person aged 13 (dc_over12_care), but for a person aged 14 or more it adds a dc_paid above zero condition the column does not state, and it inherits dc_qp's death-year error (for stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year the project checks the box and the reply does not). Project stands.

A household total is not a per-person allocation: with two people each having $1,000 expenses and $1,000 total excluded benefits, applying that same subtraction to both rows removes $2,000. The current interface supplies gross entry expenses and adjusts benefits once at form level. The existing gross-column/net-line30 choice amb.2025.dc_line30 remains recorded; this ruling makes no new owner decision or claim of per-row allocation support.

The reply is invalid: dependent.h_edu_aqee31 copies a line31 the aqee definition does not have, and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state invalid); This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading (line 30 chooses on line 28 being zero, the project's rule). By reading, the American opportunity test (dependent.edu_aoc_ok: edu, edu_1098t, edu_ein, the student's tin, lines 23 to 26) has no dependent (dependent.claimed), filer-TIN (household.all_tin) or f8863.paid condition, so it shows amounts for a student who is not your dependent, keeps the credit for a filer without a TIN (stage19.example.jack_kay with the spouse's TIN no: the project moves the student to line 31, $4,300.00), and asks dependent.edu where no expenses were paid. As the previous round. Project stands.

The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The line copies the aqee definition's line27 for every dependent entry with no condition at all: not dependent.claimed, not lines 23 to 26 (the project shows lines 27 to 30 only when dependent.edu_aoc holds), not edu or f8863.paid. A student who is not your dependent, or who was answered Yes on line 23, 24, 25 or 26 ("Stop! Go to line 31"), shows a nonzero amount on a line the filer never reaches. The worksheet arithmetic itself is the definition's. Project stands.

The reply is invalid: dependent.h_edu_aqee31 copies a line31 the aqee definition does not have, and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state invalid); This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading (line 30 chooses on line 28 being zero, the project's rule). By reading, the American opportunity test (dependent.edu_aoc_ok: edu, edu_1098t, edu_ein, the student's tin, lines 23 to 26) has no dependent (dependent.claimed), filer-TIN (household.all_tin) or f8863.paid condition, so it shows amounts for a student who is not your dependent, keeps the credit for a filer without a TIN (stage19.example.jack_kay with the spouse's TIN no: the project moves the student to line 31, $4,300.00), and asks dependent.edu where no expenses were paid. As the previous round. Project stands.

Caution: You can’t take the American opportunity credit and the lifetime learning credit for the same student in the same year"; i8863 p. 2, Who Can Claim an Education Credit: "... a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The line copies the aqee definition's line28 for every dependent entry with no condition at all: not dependent.claimed, not lines 23 to 26 (the project shows lines 27 to 30 only when dependent.edu_aoc holds), not edu or f8863.paid. A student who is not your dependent, or who was answered Yes on line 23, 24, 25 or 26 ("Stop! Go to line 31"), shows a nonzero amount on a line the filer never reaches. The worksheet arithmetic itself is the definition's. Project stands.

Caution: You can’t take the American opportunity credit and the lifetime learning credit for the same student in the same year"; i8863 p. 2, Who Can Claim an Education Credit: "... a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The line copies the aqee definition's line29 for every dependent entry with no condition at all: not dependent.claimed, not lines 23 to 26 (the project shows lines 27 to 30 only when dependent.edu_aoc holds), not edu or f8863.paid. A student who is not your dependent, or who was answered Yes on line 23, 24, 25 or 26 ("Stop! Go to line 31"), shows a nonzero amount on a line the filer never reaches. The worksheet arithmetic itself is the definition's. Project stands.

Caution: You can’t take the American opportunity credit and the lifetime learning credit for the same student in the same year"; i8863 p. 2, Who Can Claim an Education Credit: "... a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The line copies the aqee definition's line30 for every dependent entry with no condition at all: not dependent.claimed, not lines 23 to 26 (the project shows lines 27 to 30 only when dependent.edu_aoc holds), not edu or f8863.paid. A student who is not your dependent, or who was answered Yes on line 23, 24, 25 or 26 ("Stop! Go to line 31"), shows a nonzero amount on a line the filer never reaches. The worksheet arithmetic itself is the definition's. Project stands.

By reading, the American opportunity test (dependent.edu_aoc_ok: edu, edu_1098t, edu_ein, the student's tin, lines 23 to 26) has no dependent (dependent.claimed), filer-TIN (household.all_tin) or f8863.paid condition, so it shows amounts for a student who is not your dependent, keeps the credit for a filer without a TIN (stage19.example.jack_kay with the spouse's TIN no: the project moves the student to line 31, $4,300.00), and asks dependent.edu where no expenses were paid. Caution: You can’t take the American opportunity credit and the lifetime learning credit for the same student in the same year"; i8863 p. 2, Who Can Claim an Education Credit: "... a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student"; i8863 p. 9, Line 31. The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The line copies the aqee worksheet's lifetime learning line 4 (ws4_llc) for every dependent entry with no condition: not dependent.claimed, and not exclusive of lines 27 to 30, so a student for whom the American opportunity credit is figured also shows line 31, against the caution that both credits can't be taken for the same student. The project shows line 31 only when dependent.edu_llc holds. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, "A qualifying relative is your... Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)", and its last bullet, "Any other person ... who lived with you all year as a member of your household". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_edu_aqee31 copies a line31 the aqee definition does not have, and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state invalid); This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The qualifying-child test (relationship, age, own support, joint return, months of 7 or more, citizenship) and the Step 4 income and support tests follow the source, but its dependent.h_rel_qr counts sibling_descendant (a grandniece or a stepsibling's child) among the relatives who need not live with you, where Step 4 lists only a sibling's son or daughter, so a supported sibling_descendant with gross income under $5,200 who lived with you less than all year is claimed where the project, which requires 12 months and lawful for that relationship, does not. Its refusals: divorced_rule, kidnapped, married, other_claimant and sa.dependent at every entry match the project's screens (sa.dependent is refused at f1040 line 12e; scope); multiple_support now sits on dependent.qr_dep, which claimed reaches only when the qualifying-child test fails, so the previous round's refusal of a qualifying child (classm.s3.4 dep_a) no longer follows by reading. BUG-0252 and BUG-0253 reword inputs only; the reply reads the same ones. Project stands.

No. STOP You can't claim this child as a dependent". Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.deepseek.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 6,036 agree; 293 value (130 completed), 134 project-refuses, 125 project-unknown, 76 candidate-refuses (47 completed), 110 candidate-unknown. The reply validates and runs. Its errors: (1) household_member counts with any months (classm.dependent.4.deepseek dep_a, 10 months; project no, candidate yes), against the all-year bullet; sibling_descendant (a grandniece, not a listed relative) likewise counts without the all-year test; (2) the qualifying-child route omits Step 2's citizenship test (classm.f8995a.2 and classm.qdcg.2 dep_b, a child aged 3, citizen no; project no, candidate yes); (3) the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records withholding multiple_support): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply". Records with married no and joint_return yes (classm.dependent.3.deepseek and classm.dependent.5.deepseek dep_b, classm.sc.1 dep_b; project yes, candidate no) contradict the married question itself ("Was this person married at the end of 2025 ..., or is this person filing a joint return for 2025"), whose yes is refused (i1040gi p. 21, Married person); a consistent answer gives both sides the same result: representation. The project-refuses are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited screen of i1040gi p. 22 ("You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)"; classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.2), and dependent.income_exception (pp. 19-20, Exception to gross income test; classm.sc.1), all on returns the full interview refuses: scope. The project-unknown are partial records withholding an answer the interview asks of every listed person (tin, months, citizen, married, other_claimant, divorced_rule are read before any relationship branch) and older fixtures: no tax quantity differs. The candidate, like the project, counts other with 12 months without the local-law condition (finding F2, raised on the Claude log). Project stands on this log's differences.

Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.deepseek.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 4,356 agree; 1,908 value (975 completed), 405 candidate-unknown, 102 candidate-refuses (47 completed), 3 project-refuses. The candidate tests dependent.claimed instead of a qualifying child, so a qualifying relative under 17 gets the child tax credit (classm.f4952.1.deepseek, classm.f8960.1.deepseek and classm.g28.1.deepseek dep_a and dep_b, completed; an in-law aged 15; project no, candidate yes). The rest inherit its dependent.claimed: the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records withholding multiple_support): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply"; the candidate-unknown also ask gross_income and supported of a qualifying child. Project stands.

The disabled route uses months over 6, dropping the death-year rule. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`; 1,378 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,485 partial records; 7,441 comparisons): 4,426 of 7,441 agree; 1,805 value, 708 candidate-unknown, 489 candidate-refuses, 12 project-unknown, 1 project-refuses; on returns the full interview completes: 722 value, 83 candidate-refuses, 82 candidate-unknown. By reading: (1) new this round, its under-13 route is any claimed dependent under 13 (age, or 13 with dc_under13), with no qualifying-child test, so a dependent under 13 who is your qualifying relative and not your qualifying child (for example an unrelated household_member child who lived with you all year) is a qualifying person, against the quoted "qualifying child under age 13"; the project requires dependent.qc_dependent (dc_child_all_year, dc_age13). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s): "1. A qualifying child under age 13 whom you can claim as a dependent. If the child turned 13 during the year, the child is a qualifying person for the part of the year they were under age 13 ... 3. Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent"; p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_edu_aqee31 copies a line31 the aqee definition does not have, and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state invalid); This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The under-13 route now requires the qualifying child, but takes dc_under13 at any age of 13 or over, asking it of a child aged 14 or more whom the age already excludes; its disabled route requires months of 7 or more and has no death-year route, so stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (a disabled dependent parent who died in 2025, months 0, born_died yes, part_year_home yes, $4,000 of care; Form 2441 line 11 $600.00 for the project) is not a qualifying person. The missing care-expense test reaches no amount. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; on validation and on the merits. i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s): "1. A qualifying child under age 13 whom you can claim as a dependent ... 3. Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent"; p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). The line reads dependent.claimed and dependent.h_dc_would_be, both of which reach the unresolved dependent.h_qr_rel. By reading: the under-13 route now takes dc_under13 only at age 13 (the round-3 objection is fixed) but its disabled route requires months of 7 or more and has no death-year route, so stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (a disabled dependent parent who died in 2025, months 0, born_died yes, part_year_home yes, $4,000 of care; Form 2441 line 11 $600.00 for the project) is not a qualifying person. Its h_dc_would_be computes the disabled persons you could claim except for gross income, a joint return or your being claimable (i2441 p. 1, item 3), which the project refuses at f2441.nondependent_gate (scope). The missing care-expense test reaches no amount. Project stands.

Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent or could claim as a dependent except: a. The disabled person had gross income of $5,200 or more, b. The disabled person filed a joint return, or c. You (or your spouse if filing jointly) could be claimed as a dependent"; i2441 p. 1, Purpose of Form: "If you paid someone to care for your child or other qualifying person so you (or your spouse if filing jointly) could work or look for work in 2025, you may be able to take the credit for child and dependent care expenses"; p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.deepseek.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 4,165 agree; 1,451 value, 854 candidate-unknown, 295 candidate-refuses, 1 project-refuses, 8 project-unknown. (1) The sampled values are f2441.care no (classm.f4952.1.deepseek, classm.f8960.1.deepseek, classm.g28.1.deepseek, classm.sd.1.deepseek dep_c): the care omission reaches no Form 2441 amount (representation, as in round 2). (2) The disabled route requires months over 6 with no birth-or-death rule, dropping Pub. 503's (by reading, stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year, project yes): model error, as in round 3. (3) Its under-13 test is "age under 13 or dc_under13", so it asks dc_under13 of every entry aged 13 or more (the interview asks it only of a qualifying child who was 13 at the end of 2025, dependent.dc_age13) and would count a qualifying child of any age with a yes as under 13: model error. (4) The candidate-refuses inherit its dependent.claimed (multiple_support on a qualifying child, classm.s3.4.deepseek). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: collection parent binding mismatch), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. The candidate's disabled route is "dc_incapable and months > 6", with no death-year rule, though dependent.born_died and dependent.part_year_home were published (BUG-0157 added dependent.dc_lived_half after round 2, so round 2's scope ruling no longer covers the line): p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "In determining whether a person is a qualifying person, a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". Witness by reading (not executed): regression stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (BUG-0157): a disabled parent, age 80, who died in 2025, months 0 as the months question instructs for a non-qualifying-child person not with you the entire time, born_died yes, part_year_home yes, dc_incapable yes, dc_paid $4,000; the project gives dc_qp yes (dependent.dc_lived_half), 2(d) $4,000 and f2441 line 11 $600; the candidate's disabled route needs months > 6 and gives dc_qp no. Other differences: (a) its route for a disabled person who would be a dependent except for gross income or a joint return is behind the project's cited screen f2441.nondependent (i2441 p. 1, "or could claim as a dependent except"), scope; (b) it omits f2441.care, which reaches no amount (Form 2441 sums only where dc_qp holds and is not completed without care); (c) sa.dependent omission is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead); (d) its sibling_descendant variant is the odc_person error.

The corrected reply tests claimed, residence and age but does not require qualifying-child status, so an unrelated all-year QR child can be treated as a care qualifying person without incapacity. Its separate QR category omissions can also reject eligible disabled relatives. The reply contains valid age-boundary structure, but no contract cases are executed because dc_count fails types.

The reply now derives the age regimes without requiring an unnecessary dc_under13 answer and matches all ten declared qualifying-person outputs. It additionally encodes disabled would-be dependents that this project refuses through f2441.nondependent; no admission or equivalence of that excluded regime is claimed. The missing care-screen factor is irrelevant on the active care rows compared here. Its separate column(c) contract failure remains blocking.

The Test 1 conditions are the project's (relationship parent, a dependent, parent_home_paid; i1040gi p. 14, Test 1: "You paid over half the cost of keeping up a home that was the main home for all of 2025 of your parent whom you can claim as a dependent"). The dependent test omits sa.dependent, listed as a refusal gate (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead); its sibling_descendant and joint-return variants cannot reach a parent (relationship parent; a married parent is refused at dependent.qualifying_relative).

Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)", and its last bullet, "Any other person ... who lived with you all year as a member of your household". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_edu_aqee31 copies a line31 the aqee definition does not have, and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state invalid); This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The line tests claimed and part_year_home (more than half of the part of 2025 the person was alive, or since the adoption or placement) in place of the months test: for a person alive and with you all year the answer means the same, but it is an answer the source does not need where months, already asked, decides (the project reads it only for a person who fails the months test and was born, died or was placed in 2025). It also declares multiple_support on the line, refusing for a qualifying child, and inherits its claimed (a sibling_descendant who did not live with you all year). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; on validation and on the merits. i1040gi p. 14, Test 2 (a qualifying person who lived with you more than half the year, "if half or less, see Exception to time lived with you"); p501 p. 9, Death or birth: "Your qualifying child or qualifying relative who lived with you for more than half the part of the year they were alive"; i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements. The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line reads dependent.claimed, which reads dependent.h_qr_dep, so it fails validation with it; this ruling adjudicates the declaration and, separately, the tax reading by reading. By reading the residency test is months of 7 or more only, with no part-year route for a qualifying relative born or who died in 2025 (dependent.months is 12 for such a person only if your home was theirs the entire time; the project reads dependent.hoh_lived_half); its claimed branch excludes household_member and other but not sibling_descendant, so a sibling_descendant qualifying relative counts, where Test 2 takes a qualifying relative only if related as listed (the project excludes it); and the line declares multiple_support (and divorced_rule) on itself, refusing a qualifying child whose support was shared. Its third branch (a married qualifying child who is not your dependent, with sa.dependent yes) is Test 2 item 3, which the project refuses through dependent.married. Project stands.

The line itself fails validation (The reply is invalid: bare line references stand as list items inside test lists ("malformed expression (project schema)") in dependent.claimed, dependent.hoh_test2, dependent.eic_child, dependent.dc_qp and the helpers dependent.h_qc_base, h_qc_dependent, h_qr_relationship, h_qr_base and h_qr_dependent, so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state invalid)). By reading: p501 p. 9, Death or birth: "Your qualifying child or qualifying relative who lived with you for more than half the part of the year they were alive"; i1040gi p. 14, Test 2: "(if half or less, see Exception to time lived with you, later)". The reply requires months over 6 with no part-year route (stage8.hoh.parent.died_lived_part_year and stage8.hoh.adopted_part_year, where the project's Test 2 holds), and its qualifying-child branches require dependent.claimed to be no, so a claimed sibling_descendant child (a niece or nephew, outside its listed relationships) fails Test 2; the household.home_cost conjunct duplicates household.test2_met (representation). Project stands.

As last round the reply requires more than 6 months of everyone and has no part-year route (born_died, placed, part_year_home were published), so a parent who died after living with the filer for more than half of the part of the year she was alive (stage8.hoh.parent.died_lived_part_year, stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year) does not qualify the filer. Its divorced_rule and multiple_support exclusions are refusals in the project (scope).

This affects the transitive dependency of this line. The raw response is preserved, not silently repaired. BUG-0129 records that the comparer erases the annotation; .transcription/constant-unit-erasure-witness.json confirms the false-agreement mechanism. This is a model IR error, not a project tax-value finding. The separate transcription qualification hold remains in force.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on admitted eligible-TIN facts; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Steps4-5 requires the same QR income/support/residency/all-year relationship conditions and ODC citizenship/household identification conditions. The reply places dependent.tin inside claimed instead of as a separate ODC factor; both are true on admitted identified dependents. Its MFJ/claimable-filer branch extends a refused regime, and lack-of-dependent-TIN refusal placement differs; neither excluded regime is admitted by this ruling. The separate HOH and care-box defects remain pending.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 and Step5 require the all-year household route for otherwise eligible other/sibling_descendant relationships and identification for both filers when jointly filing. The corrected reply QR helper excludes those relationships outright and its ODC predicate omits household.all_tin. An eligible all-year distant relative can be wrongly rejected, and the filer-TIN prerequisite is not encoded. Invalid dc_count is a separate form-level failure, not a reason to treat these source omissions as equivalence.

These are source/interface omissions, not equivalence or new owner scope choices.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; f1040s8812 line 7, "Multiply line 6 by $500"; inherited from odc_person (same 2,552 records). i1040gi p. 19, Step 5 (the credit for other dependents for a dependent who is not a Step 3 child). Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.deepseek.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 4,222 agree; 2,126 value (1,099 completed), 183 candidate-unknown, 76 candidate-refuses, 134 project-refuses, 33 project-unknown. The test is the project's, but it excludes the candidate's ctc_child, which wrongly includes qualifying relatives under 17, so those relatives lose the $500 credit (the ctc_child witnesses, mirrored), and its dependent.claimed adds the errors ruled there (household_member and sibling_descendant without the all-year test, no citizenship test on the child route; the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records withholding multiple_support): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply"). The project-refuses are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited screen of i1040gi p. 22 ("You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)"; classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.2), and dependent.income_exception (pp. 19-20, Exception to gross income test; classm.sc.1), all on returns the full interview refuses: scope. The project-unknown are partial records withholding an answer the interview asks of every listed person (tin, months, citizen, married, other_claimant, divorced_rule are read before any relationship branch) and older fixtures: no tax quantity differs. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the returned h_qr_relationship treats sibling_descendant as an unconditional listed Step4 relative and omits other even with twelve household months. The published input defines sibling_descendant as more distant descendants (for example grandnieces and a stepsibling child); listed nieces/nephews are already in sibling. i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 requires the all-year household condition for these other relationships; p501 p.19 excludes foster parents from listed parents. On the saved seven-month distant-relative case the project gives ODC false/$0, the actual model gives true/$500; an all-year other household member reverses that error. The actual-expression witness is .transcription/dependent-age-claude-witness.json. Untyped Count constants are an additional model IR defect (BUG-0129), not an excuse to call the trees equivalent.

The line now has the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin) and the project's other Step 5 tests, but it inherits its claimed (a sibling_descendant who did not live with you all year gets $500) and its ctc_child (a child on a joint return where only the spouse has an SSN valid for employment gets $500 instead of the child tax credit). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; on validation and on the merits. i1040gi p. 19, Step 5, question 1: "Did you, and your spouse if filing a joint return, have either an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date". The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line reads dependent.claimed, which reads dependent.h_qr_dep, so it fails validation with it; this ruling adjudicates the declaration and, separately, the tax reading by reading. By reading it has no filers' TIN test (its note leaves it to the return level, where the project tests household.all_tin on this line) and inherits its dependent.ctc_child (a child on a joint return where only the spouse has an SSN valid for employment gets $500 instead of the child tax credit). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on admitted eligible-TIN facts; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Steps4-5 requires the same QR income/support/residency/all-year relationship conditions and ODC citizenship/household identification conditions. The reply places dependent.tin inside claimed instead of as a separate ODC factor; both are true on admitted identified dependents. Its MFJ/claimable-filer branch extends a refused regime, and lack-of-dependent-TIN refusal placement differs; neither excluded regime is admitted by this ruling. The separate HOH and care-box defects remain pending.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 and Step5 require the all-year household route for otherwise eligible other/sibling_descendant relationships and identification for both filers when jointly filing. The corrected reply QR helper excludes those relationships outright and its ODC predicate omits household.all_tin. An eligible all-year distant relative can be wrongly rejected, and the filer-TIN prerequisite is not encoded. Invalid dc_count is a separate form-level failure, not a reason to treat these source omissions as equivalence.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: "collection parent binding mismatch", a sum over the dependent collection inside a dependent entry), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. i1040gi p. 19, Step 5, question 1, and p. 17, Before you begin: "If you want to claim the credit for other dependents, you, and your spouse if filing jointly, must have either an SSN or ITIN". The reply drops the filer identification test it had last round (household.all_tin), and inherits its dependent.claimed: The reply's dependent.claimed (inlined) counts sibling_descendant (a grandniece or a step sibling's child, not a Step 4 listed relative; the enum gloss says it is "a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year") as a listed relative with no all-year test, against i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household"; it turns the project's divorced_rule, married and other_claimant refusals into a plain no, and it drops dependent.tin, which the project screens (dependent.claimed_no_tin, i1040gi p. 22, "You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)").

The reply omits the ODC citizenship and household.all_tin tests, and its QR relationship helper omits sibling_descendant even when the person meets the all-year household condition. The published enum reserves that category for more distant relatives; a lawful all-year eligible person may qualify under Step4. These are source/interface omissions, not equivalence or new owner scope choices.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 19, Step 5 (the credit for other dependents for a dependent who is not a Step 3 child). Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/dependent.deepseek.json; 1,222 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 2,111 partial records; 6,774 comparisons): 4,222 agree; 2,126 value (1,099 completed), 183 candidate-unknown, 76 candidate-refuses, 134 project-refuses, 33 project-unknown. The test is the project's, but it excludes the candidate's ctc_child, which wrongly includes qualifying relatives under 17, so those relatives lose the $500 credit (the ctc_child witnesses, mirrored), and its dependent.claimed adds the errors ruled there (household_member and sibling_descendant without the all-year test, no citizenship test on the child route; the candidate refuses dependent.multiple_support on every entry, including a qualifying child, whose dependency has no support test of the filer (classm.s3.4 and classm.s3.4.deepseek dep_a, a child aged 2, completed returns; generated 126, 186, 243), and needs that answer for a qualifying child (partial records withholding multiple_support): model error, i1040gi p. 21, Multiple support agreements: "If no one person contributed over half of the support of your relative (or a person who lived with you all year as a member of your household) but you and another person(s) provided more than half of your relative's support, special rules may apply"). The project-refuses are dependent.claimed_no_tin, the cited screen of i1040gi p. 22 ("You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)"; classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.2), and dependent.income_exception (pp. 19-20, Exception to gross income test; classm.sc.1), all on returns the full interview refuses: scope. The project-unknown are partial records withholding an answer the interview asks of every listed person (tin, months, citizen, married, other_claimant, divorced_rule are read before any relationship branch) and older fixtures: no tax quantity differs. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: collection parent binding mismatch), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. (1) The candidate omits the filer SSN-or-ITIN test (household.all_tin: every person has a TIN or applied for an ITIN): i1040gi p. 19, Step 5: "1. Did you, and your spouse if filing a joint return, have either an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)? ... No. STOP You can't claim the credit for other dependents"; p. 17, Before you begin: "If you want to claim the credit for other dependents, you, and your spouse if filing jointly, must have either an SSN or ITIN"; a filer with no SSN or ITIN gets $500 per other dependent where the source gives none. (2) Its qualifying-relative route treats sibling_descendant as a relative who need not live with you all year: i1040gi p. 19, Step 4: a qualifying relative is your "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" or "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household" (a grandniece or a stepsibling's child, the project's sibling_descendant, is not in the relationship list). (3) Omitting sa.dependent (listed as a refusal gate) is scope: the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead. (4) Its added "dependent.joint_return is no" on the qualifying-relative route is representation, because dependent.qualifying_relative refuses on dependent.married (i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, question 3, "See Married person").

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the returned h_qr_relationship treats sibling_descendant as an unconditional listed Step4 relative and omits other even with twelve household months. The published input defines sibling_descendant as more distant descendants (for example grandnieces and a stepsibling child); listed nieces/nephews are already in sibling. i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 requires the all-year household condition for these other relationships; p501 p.19 excludes foster parents from listed parents. On the saved seven-month distant-relative case the project gives ODC false/$0, the actual model gives true/$500; an all-year other household member reverses that error. The actual-expression witness is .transcription/dependent-age-claude-witness.json. Untyped Count constants are an additional model IR defect (BUG-0129), not an excuse to call the trees equivalent.

The reply is invalid: dependent.h_qr_dep and dependent.h_dc_would_be reference dependent.h_qr_rel, which does not resolve (the reply defines dependent.h_rel_qr), and dependent.dc_count is a sum_over of the dependent collection inside a dependent entry ("collection parent binding mismatch"), so triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/dependent.deepseek.json`, state candidate invalid). This line and the lines it reads validate; ruled on the merits by reading. The expression is unchanged from round 3: the project's choose on ptc_files, with zero spelled as $0.00 minus $0.00 (dependent.h_zero_dollars). Project stands.
